name: Kalasungsang
description: A star 49 parsecs away, 20 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71053: radius 19.67 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 124.469 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.058) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71053: effective temperature 4350 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.056)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.8 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 10 published values span log g 1.2 to 2.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71053: distance 49.092 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 49 parsecs away, 20 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 124 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,350 K, so 19.67 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 71053: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Rho Boötis
quotes.card: Rho Boötis, Latinised from ρ Boötis and formally named Kalasungsang, is a single, orange-hued star in the northern constellation of Boötes.
quotes.introduction: This star is visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of 3.59.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1284537517514584704 (quality A), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
